## Check definitions
Each template is a falsification attempt rendered as SQL. Params reference views and columns by their catalog names. A template marked [domain law: X] encodes a conservation law of domain X and decides which candidate occupies a business object; the rest are generic data checks that hold in any domain.
- anti_join: required [child, child_column, parent, parent_column]; optional [canonical, expectation]
- attribute_contradiction: required [left, left_attr, left_key, right, right_attr, right_key]; optional [canonical]
- balance: [domain law: finance]; required [amount, journal]; exactly one of [group_column, group_expr]; NOTE: amount is a BARE COLUMN NAME, never an expression — the template reads it as a number and sums it itself, so a text-typed amount column needs no cast from you; group_expr, if used, is a row-level expression
- cardinality: required [child, child_column, parent, parent_column]
- coverage: required [expected, table, unit_column]; optional [canonical]; VALUES: expected is the VALUES that must all appear in unit_column, as a list, e.g. ["DE", "US"] — NOT the column or view they live in
- decode: required [column, decode, encoded, key, pairs]; VALUES: pairs is a list of {part_expr, decode_column} objects, not identifiers
- duplicate: required [key_columns, table]
- grain: required [key_columns, table]
- ic_symmetry: [domain law: finance]; required [left, left_period, right, right_period]
- range_join: required [range_from, range_to, ranges, table, value_column]; optional [where]
- reconciliation: required [left, left_group_expr, left_measure_expr, right, right_group_expr, right_measure_expr]; optional [left_where, right_where]; NOTE: group/measure params are row-level SQL expressions over the named view; the template applies SUM itself — never pre-aggregate. This one differs from balance and subledger_equals_gl on purpose: a measure here may be any row-level arithmetic, so the template cannot know which column carries the number and cannot convert it for you. Check the column types in the view schemas: text-typed numeric columns must be cast in the expression, e.g. CAST(col AS DOUBLE)
- subledger_equals_gl: [domain law: finance]; required [account, accounts, journal, journal_amount, subledger, subledger_amount]; NOTE: subledger_amount and journal_amount are BARE COLUMN NAMES, never expressions — the template reads each as a number and sums it itself, so a text-typed amount column needs no cast from you. `account` and `accounts` are different kinds of thing and easy to swap: `account` is the COLUMN on the journal carrying the account identifier, `accounts` the account numbers to filter it to; VALUES: accounts is the account NUMBERS that make up the general-ledger side, as a list of integers, e.g. [1200] — NOT the chart-of-accounts view. Which numbers those are is domain knowledge; if the profiles do not tell you, answer template: null and say so
- validity_join: required [key_column, table, valid_from, valid_to]
Param values are bare view/column identifiers, EXCEPT where a template above marks a param VALUES (it holds data, not names) and except params whose name says expression (*_expr) or filter (*where).
